experiments.name: warp-cooperative Return address gather
experiments.validation: EP8/EP16 129-token full repeated FWD and all 96 prefix files byte-identical to historical goldens.
experiments.finding: No measured throughput gain: EP8 Return remains about 103 GB/s. Instrumented address-read time attribution requires hardware sampling before concluding metadata is the bottleneck.

experiments.name: Dense final Return contribution layout, push only
experiments.finding: Initial EP8 t129 retained-state repeated-output check failed. Pure and non-retained production repeated-output checks passed. Final output dumps in both modes match golden; root cause of intermittent failure unresolved. Large performance screen deferred.

repeat_audit.finding: Retained-state EP8 t129 failure reproduced between first and second execution. Stable baseline and rejected address-gather candidate each passed 20 repetitions with the same settings.

root_cause_investigation.finding: After kernel completion, contributions and saved X/AB are byte-identical between executions; occasional final tokens differ. The compute scheduler can run opportunistic Reduce while GEMM tasks remain; that helper still used route-major indexing. Candidate updated to map both Reduce implementations; revalidation pending.

experiments.name: Cooperative fanout metadata stores on receive Dispatch
experiments.validation: EP16 t129 20 repeated outputs and 64 golden files exact.
experiments.finding: No benefit: EP16 64K Dispatch 29.70 GB/s versus stable baseline 30.16 GB/s.

experiments.name: Bounded receive channel probes
experiments.finding: EP16 64K Dispatch remains 30.02 GB/s; no measured throughput gain. Small retained-state repeated FWD passed.

experiments.name: Chunk-wide cooperative Dispatch packing metadata

experiments.finding: Adjacent EP16 64K pure pair: Dispatch 30.04 -> 31.34 GB/s (+4.3%); total communication GPU 32.335 -> 31.894 ms; allocation-inclusive wall 34.309 -> 33.690 ms. Separate first screen 31.71 GB/s. EP16 8K full FWD GPU 5.358 ms, wall 6.711 ms; prior stable checkpoint 5.539 / 6.914 ms is historical, not an adjacent full pair. Goal not achieved.

experiments.name: Dense push Return with both Reduce paths mapped
experiments.validation: EP8 and EP16 retained-state t129, 20 repetitions; 96 prefix files byte-identical to golden.
experiments.finding: EP8 64K Return 330.24 GB/s vs baseline 102.64 GB/s; Dispatch 272.61 GB/s. EP16 Dispatch regresses to 27.33 GB/s; Return RDMA stays 45.46 GB/s. Experimental layout not yet adopted or broadly validated.
experiments.next_change: Cross-node Dispatch does not need to transmit a compact Return ordinal: its results return by GIN route IDs, and the source maps them locally. Remove that redundant metadata work and combine cooperative packing.

experiments.name: Dense final push Return layout; clean validated version
experiments.invariants: Same push payload bytes and full TMA completion protocol. Both reduction paths preserve route summation order. Validation exports preserve route-major contribution order.

experiments.name: Split GIN receive and local transport warps
experiments.finding: Dispatch 31.29 -> 29.60 GB/s; Return 45.07 -> 45.58 GB/s. Retest split with local row prefetch before rejecting domain separation.

experiments.name: Split receive prefetch and GIN row alignment screens
experiments.finding: Split+prefetch further regresses to 28.15 GB/s. Alignment gives 31.29 GB/s vs adjacent 30.83; insufficient benefit to adopt a wire-layout change without further evidence.

experiments.name: Two NVLink TMA issuers per warp
experiments.finding: Same shared memory footprint and two issuers per warp instead of one pipelined issuer. Dispatch 31.69 -> 31.37 GB/s; no gain.

experiments.name: Partition relay CTAs between local and GIN receive copy domains
experiments.pending: Production training validation and local ratio/prefetch screen
experiments.finding: 50% local CTA share: Dispatch 31.49 -> 35.79 GB/s, Return 45.73 GB/s. 67% share: Dispatch 35.66 GB/s. Every physical CTA retains math workers; copy domains retain two warps per task.

experiments.name: Relay CTA ratio and prefetch follow-up
experiments.finding: 50% local: 36.02 GB/s; 33% local: 29.21; 50% with local prefetch: 35.27. Keep 50% without local prefetch for subsequent experiments.

experiments.name: Clean static relay CTA partition across both models
experiments.finding: All tested numerical checks pass. Qwen EP16 8K full FWD regresses from 5416.735 to 5803.775 us despite faster Dispatch. Do not adopt static ownership: rejoin both Return workloads after each CTA finishes Dispatch. Flash EP16 64K pure Dispatch reaches 43.21 GB/s, but EP16 8K remains below goal in both directions.

experiments.name: Return handoff and dense GIN Dispatch packet columns
experiments.finding: Handoff preserves 35.70 GB/s pure Dispatch, but full Qwen EP16 8K remains slower (5758.51 vs 5360.34 us). Dense packet columns alone give no bandwidth improvement. Inspect Return work during Dispatch and production register allocation next.

experiments.name: Control register quota and shared Return during Dispatch
experiments.finding: Neither legal control quota 72 nor sharing Return throughout Dispatch removes full Forward regression. Retain incumbent worker scheduling; investigate message granularity and bulk payload packing.

experiments.name: Smaller GIN chunks and contiguous-token packing
experiments.finding: On incumbent worker scheduling, coalesced dense packing at 128 rows does not improve Qwen EP16 8K Dispatch (23.36 vs 23.47 GB/s). 32/16-row messages with depth16 regress Dispatch and Return; original packet format at 32 rows also regresses. Reject these candidates; isolate ring depth at unchanged 128 rows next.

experiments.name: Ring depth and continuously staggered fanout
experiments.finding: Neither ring depth16 at unchanged 128 rows nor continuous fanout prefetch improves Qwen EP16 8K/64K. 64K Dispatch baseline31.21, depth16 30.96, streaming31.01 GB/s. Keep depth8 and original fanout prefetch.

experiments.name: Partition GIN fanout tasks independently of network packet size
experiments.finding: 32-row fanout sub-batches keep 128-row network messages and return credit after the last sub-batch. Qwen EP16 8K Dispatch improves23.49->28.86 GB/s,64K31.40->33.88. Independently local Dispatch batch64 improves64K to35.54 GB/s. Full Forward validation and read-only empty-channel polling/combined candidates pending.

Combined configurations and BWD checks pending. Qwen EP16 BWD t129 also passes160 golden files includingdW1/dW2.

experiments.name: Read-only receive polling combined with larger local Dispatch batches
experiments.finding: Qwen EP16 8K Dispatch23.59->31.26 GB/s for RX32/local64 and32.58 for RX16/local64;64K31.38->37.65 and37.19 respectively. Return remains39.4-39.6 GB/s at8K and45.6-45.7 at64K. Use RX32/local64 for next full Forward and Flash checks.

diagnostics.name: Nsight Compute single-rank PC sampling
diagnostics.result: timeout; no report generated; excluded from evidence
diagnostics.cleanup: No GPU processes remained when rechecked before compact-layout experiments.

diagnostics.name: Baseline EP16 64K communication timeline
diagnostics.finding: Packing remains active until just before the final Dispatch submissions. Receiving fanout contributes about 353 us after the last submission on this rank. These are same-GPU timestamps, not cross-node wire latency.

diagnostics.name: Dispatch and Return RDMA issue overlap
diagnostics.finding: Zero Return payload submitted before final Dispatch submission on all 16 ranks. Pure benchmark intentionally sequences Dispatch and Return. No D/R NIC contention explains low Dispatch rate.

diagnostics.name: Dispatch payload ablation
diagnostics.finding: Baseline Dispatch 8611.295 us; omit local and relay NVLink payload 6486.305 us; omit GIN Dispatch packing payload 8539.185 us. Prioritize NVLink copy/relay path over sender packing. All protocol/metadata work retained; payload correctness intentionally absent in ablations.

diagnostics.name: Separate local Dispatch and received fanout payload ablations
diagnostics.finding: No local Dispatch payload: 6822.685 us. No received fanout payload: 6662.960 us. Complete baseline: 8471.105 us. Both NVLink workloads contribute to the throughput limit.

diagnostics.name: Static resource and local-memory instruction audit
diagnostics.finding: Baseline and handoff EP16 retained Forward entries both report REG 168, STACK 656, LOCAL 0. After control register deallocation, static LDL/STL counts change from 2701/1396 to 2710/1401. These counts include stack/structure accesses and do not establish dynamic spill cost. Test the legal 72-register control quota and shared Return work during Dispatch.

diagnostics.name: Return queue confirmation and completion-tail timeline
diagnostics.finding: Confirmation waiting decreases in the regressive combined variant; it does not explain the regression. Last-snapshot timelines show median last receive/NVLink-copy event to transport-worker-exit intervals616.656/551.056us. Test notification closure using final data tails instead of empty End packets. Trace timestamps are compared only within each GPU; instrumented latency is not production throughput. This interval can include outstanding outbound GIN completion/credits; it is not all attributable to notification End packets.

diagnostics.name: GIN drain reasons and final flush timing
diagnostics.finding: Qwen EP16 8K pure communication profiling, RX32. Last context reason is remote credit8ranks or locally unsubmitted ACK8ranks. Per-rank maximum flush52.45-65.41us; all128context flush statistics above. baseline/candidate64prefix files exact,12repeats. Trace is diagnostic only; subsequent targeted peer flush retains all mapped peer queue completion. No attribution of the entire tail to flush or terminal packets.
